messages.subject: Defining PC prior - pc.cor1
parts:
Hi,

I am analyzing annual biomass time-series data (at replicate plots) and making using of INLA's ar1 model. So far I have been using default priors, but I would like to check my results with a PC prior on the ar1 model.

Following the guidance here (https://haakonbakka.bitbucket.io/btopic115.html#61_what_is_pc_prior), I need to set priors for theta 1 and theta 2 as follows. where I need to decide on u and alpha.

hyper <- list(theta1 = list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(u, alpha)),
                    theta2 = list(prior="pc.cor1", param=c(u, alpha))

formula <- y ~ f(iYear,model='ar1',hyper=hyper)

For the pc.prec parameters, I have seen several sources select the u and alpha as (3 * sd of response data, 0.01).

For the pc.cor1 parameters, the documentation shows that P( rho > u) = alpha. But I am still unsure what are reasonable values for u and alpha. In the model with default priors (shown below), rho is estimated as 0.67. Given the type of data being analysed, I don't expect the ar1 correlation to be particularly high but that it is still present.

Any advice on what would be reasonable alpha and u for the pc.cor1 would be much appreciated!

Cheers,

Diana

Here is my full model and output with default priors

inlaRealm <- inla(Biomass ~ cYear + cYear:Realm + #realm-specific trends

                f(Plot_ID_4INLA,model='iid')+#random intercept

                f(Plot_ID_4INLAR,iYear,model='iid')+ #random slopes

                f(iYear,model='ar1',replicate=Plot_ID),#ar1 at each plot

              control.predictor = list(link = 1),

              data=mydf)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Defining PC prior - pc.cor1
parts:
thanks for your email.

btw, there is a spesific random-intercept-slop model available,see
inla.doc("intslope") which you might find useful.

about the AR1, it depends on if the AR1 model is there as a 'random
effect' that is possible correlated, OR, as a possible 'mean
correction'. In the first case, you might consider pc.cor0, and in the
second case pc.cor1.

About u,alpha. It think of

> sqrt(3)/2
[1] 0.8660254038

as half-way between independence and full dependence, as then the
conditional stdev is sqrt(1-rho^2) = 1/2 which is rho = sqrt(3)/2, if
rho > 0.

so maybe u = sqrt(3)/2 and alpha = 3/4 ?

H
